H2C4#0.quote: Of particular interest at Chitkul are its houses with either slate or wooden plank roofs, a Buddhist temple and a small tower.

H2C1#0.quote: Last inhabited village on the Indo-Tibet border, Chitkul in Baspa valley is 25 km from Sangla. The motorable road ends at this village and any further journey has to be done on foot.

H2C3#0.quote: During winters, the place mostly remains covered with snow and the inhabitants move to lower regions of Himachal.

H2C2#0.quote: slopes of the highlands around the village sliced into terraced fields, a crystal clear River Baspa flowing through bestows immense beauty

H2C2#1.quote: The village has nice small temple dedicated to goddess Mathi

H2C2#2.quote: Camping by the river can evoke spirituality.

H2N1#0.quote: April to October is a good time to visit Kinnaur. In winters, starting from November, the temperature starts to fall and they do drop well below the freezing point in December and January.

H2T6#0.quote: Open fires are forbidden within GHNP.

H2T6#1.quote: Always find your next campsite well before sunset.

H2T6#3.quote: Modest attire must be worn at all times within GHNP and the ecozone.

H2G1#0.quote: The park was established in 1984 and is spread over an area of 1171 km2; elevations within the park range between 1500 and 6000 m.

H2G1#1.quote: In June 2014, the Great Himalayan National Park was added to the UNESCO list of World Heritage Sites

H2G2#0.quote: Home to the rare and endangered Himalayan Thar, Himalayan Brown Bear, Snow Leopard and Blue Sheep, the park is a refuge to Western Tragopan, Monal and other rare birds also.

H2G2#1.quote: there are no roads or paved trails in this carefully conserved natural habitat

H2J2#0.quote: Several buses cross the pass regularly during the summer months. In winters the pass receives a lot of snow and remains closed for traffic from December to March.

H2J1#0.quote: A wind swept commanding pass, Jalori demarcates the catchments of River Satluj from Beas.

H2J1#1.quote: The panoramic view captures snow clad Himalayan ranges in the distance, deep forests of the Great Himalayan National Park

H2J1#2.quote: A day hike to Serolsar Lake is a memorable trail to tread upon.

H2J3#0.quote: Shoja is also the base for easy treks to Jalori Pass, Serolsar Lake, Takrasi and Khanag.

H2K1#0.quote: Overlooking Sangla village stands the towering hill fort of Kamru. This wood and stone structure was the original seat of power of the rulers of Kinnaur.

H2K1#1.quote: A series of low gates in the hamlet lead to the fort that rises five stories high.

H2K1#2.quote: The stronghold has an idol of Hindu goddess Kamakhya Devi (Kamakshi) enshrined in the upper storey.

H2K3#0.quote: Sangla is situated on the right bank of Baspa river 18 Km from Karcham and 38 km from Reckongpeo.

H2K2#0.quote: The main wooden gate of the fort has the Buddha cast on it, whose blessings are sought before entering the village.

H2K2#1.quote: surrounded by fields and orchards producing some of the finest apples of Himachal

H2K2#2.quote: The village also has a Badrinath temple.

H2L2#0.quote: Nako Monastery, dated to 1025 AD, is located in the village as well as several other Buddhist chortens.

H2L2#1.quote: Nako is the largest village in the Hangrang Valley

H2L1#0.quote: At the commanding altitude of 3,662 meters, Nako village with a small lake and a highly revered Buddhist monastery has become very popular with tourists.

H2L1#1.quote: A footprint-like impression cast on a rock is ascribed to Guru Padmasambhava

H2L1#2.quote: Nako is also the base to reach Tashigang monastery and is the starting point for mountaineers setting out to scale Reo Pargial Peak.
